transcription.text:
RELATIONAL ARCHIVAL INVESTIGATION
MUSEUM OF ONE
Relational Archival Investigation · Research paper
8
These cases matter to the procedure because they prevent the inquiry from equating productivity 
with discrepancy. The same comparison can establish compatible dates, distinguish presentations, 
retain a material question, or identify a production-year difference. An adequate account reports 
what each relation supports rather than counting every difference as a discovery.
6. Park Suk-won: a genuine pair and an unwarranted third date
The Jeok–Eungnyeok case yields a different result. Acquisition entry 76 gives 1974; collection 
record 7925 gives 1972 and identifies remaking of the wooden elements in 2016. The record also 
associates the work with the First Seoul Biennale in 1974. Artist, Korean title, cloth-and-wood 
materials, cloth dimensions of 332 × 358 cm, and four closely corresponding wooden elements 
support comparison of the descriptions as accounts of one work (MMCA, 2016 Annual Report, 40; 
record 7925).
The final dimension of the fourth wooden element differs by 0.1 cm, and the variation is retained. 
A small measurement difference alone does not outweigh the conjunction of identifying details, but 
neither is it silently normalized. An accession cross-reference would strengthen the identification; 
evidence of separately identified realizations could alter its scope. The claim concerns the 
described work and its acknowledged remaking, not unchanged materials throughout its history.
Separating the 2016 intervention leaves the leading 1972/1974 contrast intact. The public 
comparison establishes different production-year assignments. It does not determine which year is 
historically correct, whether one published description directly replaced another, or why either year 
was assigned. An exhibition-associated convention, a correction, or different information available 
to the compilers remain possible explanations.
The historical stake is specific. MMCA describes wooden elements surrounding a cloth surface 
with painted shadows, producing an implausible relation between the objects and their 
representations. A 1972 production date would place this arrangement two years before its reported 
Seoul exhibition; 1974 would locate production within the exhibition year. The question is whether 
the exhibition presented an existing experiment or a more recently made work. The artist’s 
documented Myeongdong Gallery exhibition in 1974 identifies another body of contemporary 
material worth examining, but its existence does not establish that this installation appeared there 
(Arts Council Korea, artist record 1172).
The same institutional artist record lists Jeok–Eungnyeok 2, dated 1973, in wood and measuring 
240 × 40 × 25 cm. The numbered title, materials, and dimensions do not identify MMCA’s cloth-
and-four-wood arrangement. Adding 1973 to the paired dates would therefore turn a plausible 
relation among works into an unsupported identity of one work.
That exclusion is one of the investigation’s completed judgments. The 1973 record is relevant to 
the artist’s practice, but it does not supply a third production year for the MMCA installation. The 
established date difference and the rejected third-date extension have different grounds. One 
remains historically open because the needed explanation is missing; the other is withheld because 
the evidence does not establish the proposed individual identity.
Further documentation could revise either judgment. A contemporary photograph could support an 
earlier production date. An accession file could identify the basis of the museum’s assignment. A 
source linking the separately titled work to the installation could explain their relationship. Each 
would answer a particular question. None should be made to settle all aspects of the case merely 
because it concerns the same artist or series.

transcription.text:
RAI · DOCUMENTARY EVIDENCE
MUSEUM OF ONE
Relational Archival Investigation · Supplement 1
3
Evidence that could extend the account. Dated installation photographs, original negatives, or a 
material history could specify how the exhibited ensemble relates to the action and its later 
realization. Such evidence would enlarge the account of particular components rather than 
automatically alter the leading year.
B.4. C-75 — Lee Kang-so, Painting–78–1
Sources. S-M01, entry 75; S-M75, web record 7924, management number 07911. Korean title: 
“페인팅-78-1.” Additional source S-T01 is the published conversation dated 14 October 2018 (Lee 
2018).
Relevant statements. The report gives 1978 for a silent, single-channel colour video lasting 29 
minutes 25 seconds. The collection entry gives 1977 and 30 minutes, associating its first 
presentation with the fourth Daegu Contemporary Art Festival in 1978.
Identification. Artist, distinctive title, medium, and the description of painting on glass before a 
camera support the match. The differing durations are retained. They do not establish whether one 
entry is rounded or whether different transfers are described.
Testimonial explanation. S-T01 identifies production in 1977 and presentation in 1978. The 
relevant exchange begins with Cho Su-jin’s question about painting on a monitor screen; Lee 
distinguishes the two dates and calls for correction of confusion in the record. The conversation is 
dated internally to 14 October 2018. A “2021” designation in the hosted filename is not substituted 
for the conversation date.
Judgment. An attributed production–presentation chronology is supported. The reason for the 
annual report’s assignment and the history of an institutional amendment remain separate 
questions. Artist recollection is not treated as an acquisition-file record. The duration question 
remains unadjudicated because the recordings were not timed or compared.
B.5. C-76 — Park Suk-won, Jeok–Eungnyeok
Sources. S-M01, entry 76; S-M76, web record 7925, management number 07912. Korean title: 
“적-응력.”
Relevant statements. The report assigns 1974 in the production-year column. The collection date 
reads “1972(나무: 2016 재제작),” identifying 1972 and remaking of the wood in 2016. Its 
narrative associates the work with the First Seoul Biennale in 1974.
Identification. The artist, Korean title, oil-on-cloth and wood, cloth dimensions of 332 × 358 cm, 
and four wooden elements provide substantial descriptive correspondence. No common 
management number is printed in both witnesses. The comparison identifies the described work 
rather than certifying the uninterrupted identity of every material component.
Measurements. The report gives wooden elements of 64 × 25 × 26; 65.5 × 25.5 × 27; 61.5 × 25.4 
× 25.4; and 63.5 × 25 × 25.1 cm. The collection entry gives the same cloth and first three 
component measurements, with 63.5 × 25 × 25 cm for the last. The 0.1 cm difference is preserved.
Judgment. The leading production-year assignments differ after remaking has been distinguished. 
The identification is supported at the work-description level. Neither source establishes the correct 
production year independently, the cause of the difference, or the date of a catalogue amendment. 
Section C records the alternatives.

transcription.text:
RAI · DOCUMENTARY EVIDENCE
MUSEUM OF ONE
Relational Archival Investigation · Supplement 1
5
C. The Jeok–Eungnyeok inquiry
C.1. A comparison that remains warranted
J-P01 — identification. Retain the pairing in C-76 as a supported comparison of descriptions of 
one work. Its grounds are the conjunction of artist, title, material arrangement, and dimensions. The 
remaking statement limits what the identification says about physical continuity.
J-P02 — documentary difference. Retain 1974 and 1972 as different leading production-year 
assignments. The separate 2016 date explains the later materials but leaves that contrast intact. The 
result concerns the published descriptions, not yet the historical truth of either production year.
Historical consequence. A 1972 production date places the installation two years before its 
reported 1974 Seoul presentation. A 1974 date places production in the exhibition year. This is a 
conditional difference in the work’s chronology. No subsequent critical argument has been shown 
to have changed because of either institutional assignment.
C.2. Alternative explanations
H-P01 — different conventions. One description may use an exhibition-associated year and the 
other an earlier production year. The collection narrative supplies a relevant 1974 exhibition. The 
report’s production-year heading means that an editorial convention or object-specific explanation 
is still required.
H-P02 — correction. One assignment may correct a mistake. A dated worksheet, annotation, 
curatorial account, or explicit testimony connecting the assignments would support that 
explanation. No responsible person or motive is inferred from the differing years.
H-P03 — different historical information. The compilers may have drawn on different testimony 
or documents. The relevant source and its connection to the assignment would have to be 
established. Later consultation is not evidence of better historical knowledge.
H-P04 — related but distinct realizations. The records may concern differently identified 
realizations despite their correspondences. That alternative is less persuasive at the level of the 
work descriptions, but photographs or accession documentation could require reconsideration. The 
small measurement variation alone does not establish it.
J-P03 — explanation. Retain H-P01–H-P03 as open explanations of the assignments and H-P04 
as a possible challenge to the scope of identification. The observed difference is not rewritten as a 
documented administrative amendment.
C.3. The separately numbered 1973 work
S-P03. Arts Council Korea, DA-Arts artist record 1172, work list and exhibition chronology. The 
work list records “積(적)-응력2,” 1973, wood, 240 × 40 × 25 cm. The chronology also lists a 1974 
Myeongdong Gallery solo exhibition without identifying the MMCA installation among its 
exhibits.
J-P04 — exclusion from the individual chronology. The numbered title, medium, and 
dimensions do not identify MMCA’s cloth-and-four-wood arrangement. The entry is relevant to a 
related series or practice, but it does not presently supply a third date for the same individual work.
Evidence that could alter the account. A source explicitly connecting the 1973 work with the

dossiers.title: Park Suk-won (박석원): a documentary date difference and the limit of a third date
dossiers.question: What does the comparison of the 1972 and 1974 assignments establish, and why does the separately numbered 1973 work not supply a third date for the same installation?
dossiers.summary: Two institutional descriptions support a qualified work-description comparison and a production-year difference. The correct historical year and cause remain open. A separately numbered 1973 work is not established as the same individual installation.
dossiers.limitations: Images are authentic pages of the author’s published research, not original institutional manuscripts. The main paper and supplement belong to one research programme and are not independent corroborating witnesses. Original-source records are linked separately.
